nv_children_s_crag.blurb: A small trad-only cliff in the Willow Spring section of Red Rock, about 4,600 feet up. Ten single-pitch lines on sandstone climb dihedrals, cracks and smooth faces, with grades running from roughly 5.6 up to a single 5.11, so most of the wall suits moderate leaders. The face catches little sun, particularly after midday, which makes it a comfortable pick when other walls are baking. The walk from the dirt-road end of the lot is short, around five minutes, and single-pitch lines finish with an easy walk-off to the right. Bring a standard rack and expect a quiet day on a modest wall.

nv_church_pew_the.blurb: A compact sport crag on a narrow ledge high on the Cathedral Rock side of Kyle Canyon, up on Mount Charleston at around 8,100 feet. Ten bolted lines, with a stick clip left for the first bolt, run from low 5.10 through the 5.11s to a few 5.12s, so it is a place for strong sport climbers rather than beginners. Getting there means a scrambly, cairn-marked traverse across scree chutes and a wall, and an injury has happened on it, so go carefully. Each route has lower-off bolts, and the day usually ends with a rappel off the ledge. The mountain elevation keeps it cooler than the valley.

nv_coco_crag.blurb: A shaded crag in the Red Spring part of Calico Basin, near Las Vegas, with ten routes on good dark sandstone. The mix is six sport lines, three trad and one top-rope, mostly vertical or slabby, and the grades range from about 5.6 up to the low 5.11s, with a decent cluster in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The wall sits out of the sun from mid-morning, so it is pleasant on warm days. The base is roughly a 15-minute uphill walk from the Red Springs lot, with the wall visible the entire way. It combines easily with neighboring small crags.

nv_dante_s_wall.blurb: A tall, fairly hidden wall in the First Pullout zone of Red Rock, close to Calico Basin and above 4,000 feet. It holds ten routes, nine of them sport and one a trad line, and the bulk of the sport lines fall at 5.10 with a lone 5.9 and one 5.12. Styles change a lot across the wall, from a varnished chimney to steeper, crimpy and bouldery pulling. Reaching it takes around 20 minutes of cairn-following and a short steep slot, so it is not a quick stop. A good choice for solid 5.10 climbers wanting something different from the roadside walls.

nv_potato_chip.blurb: A fairly large boulder in the main cluster of the Kraft Boulders, in Calico Basin near Las Vegas. Its half-moon, overhanging north face stays in the shade all day, while the back side warms up with sun until late afternoon. The ten problems here are mostly low to middle grades, mainly V1 and V2 with a handful of harder ones up to V8, and the front holds the popular crimpy overhanging lines. Landings are good and a pad is the only protection needed. The boulder sits roughly halfway into the field, close to the main trail, a short walk from the road.

nv_frock_rock.blurb: A sizeable tower standing near the middle of the valley floor at Christmas Tree Pass, west of Laughlin, also known as Nixon Tower. The climbing is trad on quartz monzonite, with ten routes mostly around 5.10 and a few easier or harder, and at least one is a three-pitch outing. The tower sits near the neighboring dome, and the approach starts from the same gate-side parking, bearing up and left instead of up and right. This is a lightly visited desert spot, so bring a full rack and expect solitude. Summer here is brutal; plan on winter days.

nv_sonic_youth_wall.blurb: A sport-only wall in the Wake Up Wall area of Red Rock's Sandstone Quarry, northwest of the quarry lot. All ten routes here are bolted and hard: half sit in the 5.11 range and half in the 5.12 range, so this is not a place for newcomers. The wall faces northeast, which keeps the shade in the cooler months. To get there, follow the Turtlehead Peak trail from the parking area, then step off to the left toward the cliffs. It pairs naturally with the neighboring Wake-Up Wall for a day of pocketed and crimpy sandstone sport climbing.
